q-161204.name: Question 1
q-161204.problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with normal vector $\overset{~}{n},$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨z,\,xy,\,{y}^{2}-1⟩\,,\,\overset{~}{n}(x,y,z)=⟨{y}^{2},\,2x,\,-z⟩\,,\,n=\frac{\overset{~}{n}}{‖\overset{~}{n}‖}.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}\frac{2{x}^{2}y+z}{\boxed{}}\,\text{d}S
$$

what is the missing expression?
q-161204.worked_solution:
If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $F$ is continuous vector field, then the flux of $F$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

To compute the above dot product, we must normalize the vector $\overset{~}{n}.$ By doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =\frac{\overset{~}{n}}{‖\overset{~}{n}‖} \\  & =\frac{⟨{y}^{2},\,2x,\,-z⟩}{\sqrt{{({y}^{2})}^{2}+(2x)^{2}+(-z)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{⟨{y}^{2},\,2x,\,-z⟩}{\sqrt{{y}^{4}+4{x}^{2}+{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{⟨{y}^{2},\,2x,\,-z⟩}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}+{y}^{4}+{z}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculating the dot product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot n & =⟨z,\,xy,\,{y}^{2}-1⟩\cdot \frac{⟨{y}^{2},\,2x,\,-z⟩}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}+{y}^{4}+{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{⟨z,\,xy,\,{y}^{2}-1⟩\cdot ⟨{y}^{2},\,2x,\,-z⟩}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}+{y}^{4}+{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{{y}^{2}z+2{x}^{2}y-z({y}^{2}-1)}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}+{y}^{4}+{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2{x}^{2}y+z}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}+{y}^{4}+{z}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}\,\frac{2{x}^{2}y+z}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}+{y}^{4}+{z}^{2}}}\,\text{d}S.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Consider the vector field F and the surface S with normal vector n~, where

F(x,y,z)=⟨z,xy,y2−1⟩,n~(x,y,z)=⟨y2,2x,−z⟩,n=n~‖n~‖.

If the flux of F across S with respect to n is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬S2x2y+zAAAAAAAdS

what is the missing expression?

a
x2+y2+z2
b
2x2+y4−z2
c
x2+y2+z2
d
4x2+y4+z2
e
4x2+y4+z2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

If S is an oriented surface with unit normal vector n, and F is continuous vector field, then the flux of F across S measured with respect to n is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS.

To compute the above dot product, we must normalize the vector n~. By doing this, we get

n=n~‖n~‖=⟨y2,2x,−z⟩(y2)2+(2x)2+(−z)2=⟨y2,2x,−z⟩y4+4x2+z2=⟨y2,2x,−z⟩4x2+y4+z2.

Calculating the dot product, we have

F⋅n=⟨z,xy,y2−1⟩⋅⟨y2,2x,−z⟩4x2+y4+z2=⟨z,xy,y2−1⟩⋅⟨y2,2x,−z⟩4x2+y4+z2=y2z+2x2y−z(y2−1)4x2+y4+z2=2x2y+z4x2+y4+z2.

Therefore, the flux can be written as

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬S2x2y+z4x2+y4+z2dS.

q-161202.name: Question 2
q-161202.problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with unit normal vector $n,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨\frac{z}{2},\,x,\,z-y⟩\,,\,n(x,y,z)=\frac{1}{5}⟨4,\,0,\,-3⟩\,.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S=\frac{1}{5}{∬}_{S}\boxed{}\,\text{d}S,
$$

what is the missing expression?
q-161202.worked_solution:
If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $F$ is continuous vector field, then the flux of $F$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

Calculating the dot product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot n & =⟨\frac{z}{2},\,x,\,z-y⟩\cdot \frac{1}{5}⟨4,\,0,\,-3⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨\frac{z}{2},\,x,\,z-y⟩\cdot ⟨4,\,0,\,-3⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(2z+0-3(z-y)) \\  & =\frac{3y-z}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}\frac{3y-z}{5}\,\text{d}S \\  & =\frac{1}{5}{∬}_{S}3y-z\,\text{d}S.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the vector field F and the surface S with unit normal vector n, where

F(x,y,z)=⟨z2,x,z−y⟩,n(x,y,z)=15⟨4,0,−3⟩.

If the flux of F across S with respect to n is given by

∬SF⋅dS=15∬SAAAAAAAdS,

what is the missing expression?

a
y+4z
b
x+3y+z2
c
3y−z
d
x+2y−z
e
y−z
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

If S is an oriented surface with unit normal vector n, and F is continuous vector field, then the flux of F across S measured with respect to n is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS.

F⋅n=⟨z2,x,z−y⟩⋅15⟨4,0,−3⟩=15⟨z2,x,z−y⟩⋅⟨4,0,−3⟩=15(2z+0−3(z−y))=3y−z5.

Therefore, the flux can be written as

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬S3y−z5dS=15∬S3y−zdS.

Consider the vector field F and the surface S with normal vector n~, where

F(x,y,z)=⟨x2,2xz,x+y⟩,n~(x,y,z)=⟨−3z,x,2y⟩,n=n~‖n~‖.

If the flux of F across S with respect to n is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬S2xy+2y2−x2zAAAAAAAdS

what is the missing expression?

a
 x2+y2+z2
b
 x2+2y2+3z2
c
 x+2y+3z
d
 x2+4y2+9z2
e
 x2+4y2+9z2

Correct
EXPLANATION

If S is an oriented surface with unit normal vector n, and F is continuous vector field, then the flux of F across S measured with respect to n is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS.

To compute the above dot product, we must normalize the vector n~. By doing this, we get

n=n~‖n~‖=⟨−3z,x,2y⟩(−3z)2+(x)2+(2y)2=⟨−3z,x,2y⟩9z2+x2+4y2=⟨−3z,x,2y⟩x2+4y2+9z2.

Calculating the dot product, we have

F⋅n=⟨x2,2xz,x+y⟩⋅⟨−3z,x,2y⟩x2+4y2+9z2=⟨x2,2xz,x+y⟩⋅⟨−3z,x,2y⟩x2+4y2+9z2=−3x2z+2x2z+2y(x+y)x2+4y2+9z2=2xy+2y2−x2zx2+4y2+9z2.

Therefore, the flux can be written as

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬S2xy+2y2−x2zx2+4y2+9z2dS.

q-161208.problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with normal vector $\overset{~}{n},$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨2z,\,xy,\,2⟩\,,\,\overset{~}{n}(x,y,z)=⟨xy,\,-z,\,y⟩\,,\,n=\frac{\overset{~}{n}}{‖\overset{~}{n}‖}.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}\frac{xyz+2y}{\boxed{}}\,\text{d}S
$$

what is the missing expression?
q-161208.worked_solution:
If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $F$ is continuous vector field, then the flux of $F$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

To compute the above dot product, we must normalize the vector $\overset{~}{n}.$ By doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =\frac{\overset{~}{n}}{‖\overset{~}{n}‖} \\  & =\frac{⟨xy,\,-z,\,y⟩}{\sqrt{(xy)^{2}+(-z)^{2}+(y)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{⟨xy,\,-z,\,y⟩}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}+{y}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{⟨xy,\,-z,\,y⟩}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculating the dot product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot n & =⟨2z,\,xy,\,2⟩\cdot \frac{⟨xy,\,-z,\,y⟩}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{⟨2z,\,xy,\,2⟩\cdot ⟨xy,\,-z,\,y⟩}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2xyz-xyz+2y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{xyz+2y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}\,\frac{xyz+2y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}\,\text{d}S.\end{aligned}
$$

q-161208.html:
Question 4
?

Consider the vector field F and the surface S with normal vector n~, where

F(x,y,z)=⟨2z,xy,2⟩,n~(x,y,z)=⟨xy,−z,y⟩,n=n~‖n~‖.

If the flux of F across S with respect to n is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬Sxyz+2yAAAAAAAdS

what is the missing expression?

a
xy+y+z
b
 x2y2+y2+z2
c
 xy+y+z
d
 2x2+y2+z2
e
 x2y2+y2+z2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

If S is an oriented surface with unit normal vector n, and F is continuous vector field, then the flux of F across S measured with respect to n is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS.

To compute the above dot product, we must normalize the vector n~. By doing this, we get

n=n~‖n~‖=⟨xy,−z,y⟩(xy)2+(−z)2+(y)2=⟨xy,−z,y⟩x2y2+z2+y2=⟨xy,−z,y⟩x2y2+y2+z2.

Calculating the dot product, we have

F⋅n=⟨2z,xy,2⟩⋅⟨xy,−z,y⟩x2y2+y2+z2=⟨2z,xy,2⟩⋅⟨xy,−z,y⟩x2y2+y2+z2=2xyz−xyz+2yx2y2+y2+z2=xyz+2yx2y2+y2+z2.

Therefore, the flux can be written as

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬Sxyz+2yx2y2+y2+z2dS.

q-161206.name: Question 5
q-161206.problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with normal vector $\overset{~}{n},$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨y,\,-z,\,x⟩\,,\,\overset{~}{n}(x,y,z)=⟨2z,\,y,\,3{x}^{2}⟩\,,\,n=\frac{\overset{~}{n}}{‖\overset{~}{n}‖}.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}\frac{\boxed{}}{\sqrt{9{x}^{4}+{y}^{2}+4{z}^{2}}}\,\text{d}S
$$

what is the missing expression?
q-161206.worked_solution:
If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $F$ is continuous vector field, then the flux of $F$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

To compute the above dot product, we must normalize the vector $\overset{~}{n}.$ By doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =\frac{\overset{~}{n}}{‖\overset{~}{n}‖} \\  & =\frac{⟨2z,\,y,\,3{x}^{2}⟩}{\sqrt{(2z)^{2}+(y)^{2}+{(3{x}^{2})}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{⟨2z,\,y,\,3{x}^{2}⟩}{\sqrt{4{z}^{2}+{y}^{2}+9{x}^{4}}} \\  & =\frac{⟨2z,\,y,\,3{x}^{2}⟩}{\sqrt{9{x}^{4}+{y}^{2}+4{z}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculating the dot product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot n & =⟨y,\,-z,\,x⟩\cdot \frac{⟨2z,\,y,\,3{x}^{2}⟩}{\sqrt{9{x}^{4}+{y}^{2}+4{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{⟨y,\,-z,\,x⟩\cdot ⟨2z,\,y,\,3{x}^{2}⟩}{\sqrt{9{x}^{4}+{y}^{2}+4{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2yz-yz+3{x}^{3}}{\sqrt{9{x}^{4}+{y}^{2}+4{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{3}+yz}{\sqrt{9{x}^{4}+{y}^{2}+4{z}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}\,\frac{3{x}^{3}+yz}{\sqrt{9{x}^{4}+{y}^{2}+4{z}^{2}}}\,\text{d}S.\end{aligned}
$$

q-161152.name: Question 6
q-161152.problem: Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨z,\,y,\,x⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined in Cartesian coordinates as $z=1$ for $0\le x\le 1$ and $0\le y\le 1.$ Calculate the flux of $F$ through $S$ with respect to the upward-pointing unit normal vector $n.$
q-161152.worked_solution:
If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $F$ is continuous vector field, then the flux of $F$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

For the surface $z=1$ for  $0\le x\le 1$ and $0\le y\le 1,$ the upward-pointing unit normal vector is

$$
n=⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩.
$$

Using the fact that $z=1$ on $S,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot n & =⟨z,\,y,\,x⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,y,\,x⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the flux of $F$ across $S$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}x\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}x\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}x\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\text{d}y{\int }_{0}^{1}x\,\text{d}x \\  & =1\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

q-161186.name: Question 7
q-161186.problem: Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨z,\,y-x,\,x+y⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined in Cartesian coordinates as $z=2$ for $0\le x\le 1$ and $0\le y\le 1.$ Calculate the flux of $F$ through $S$ with respect to the upward-pointing unit normal vector $n.$
q-161186.worked_solution:
If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $F$ is continuous vector field, then the flux of $F$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

For the surface $z=2$ for  $0\le x\le 1$ and $0\le y\le 1,$ the upward-pointing unit normal vector is

$$
n=⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩.
$$

Using the fact that $z=2$ on $S,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot n & =⟨z,\,y-x,\,x+y⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,y-x,\,x+y⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =x+y.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the flux of $F$ across $S$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}(x+y)\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}(x+y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(x+y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+xy]}_{x=0}^{x=1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{1}{2}+y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{1}{2}\,y+\frac{1}{2}\,{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

q-161197.problem: Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨2y,\,2x,\,2z⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined in Cartesian coordinates as $z=2$ for $0\le x\le \frac{1}{2}$ and $0\le y\le \frac{1}{4}.$ Calculate the flux of $F$ through $S$ with respect to the *downward*-pointing unit normal vector $n.$

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

For the surface $z=1$ for  $0\le x\le \frac{1}{2}$ and $0\le y\le \frac{1}{4},$ the downward-pointing unit normal vector is

$$
n=⟨0,\,0,\,-1⟩.
$$

Using the fact that $z=2$ on $S,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot n & =⟨2y,\,2x,\,2z⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨2y,\,2x,\,4⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}

Therefore, we can calculate the flux of $F$ across $S$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}(-4)\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-4)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/4}{\int }_{0}^{1/2}(-4)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =-4{\int }_{0}^{1/4}\,\text{d}y{\int }_{0}^{1/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-4\cdot [y]_{0}^{1/4}\cdot [x]_{0}^{1/2} \\  & =-4\cdot \frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.

$$

$$

Since we require an upward-pointing normal vector to our surface $S,$ we must select one where the $z$-component is positive. This gives us the normal vector

$$

$$

Normalizing this vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =\frac{\overset{~}{n}}{‖\overset{~}{n}‖} \\  & =\frac{⟨1,\,-2,\,1⟩}{\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}⟨1,\,-2,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot n & =⟨z+x,\,x+y,\,2x+6⟩\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}⟨1,\,-2,\,1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}⟨2y,\,x+y,\,2x+6⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,-2,\,1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}(2y-2(x+y)+2x+6) \\  & =\frac{6}{\sqrt{6}} \\  & =\sqrt{6}.\end{aligned}

$$

$$

$$

$$

Normalizing this vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =\frac{\overset{~}{n}}{‖\overset{~}{n}‖} \\  & =\frac{⟨1,\,-4,\,-1⟩}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+(-1)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{18}}⟨1,\,-4,\,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}⟨1,\,-4,\,-1⟩.\end{aligned}

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(-x-y-1)\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(-x-y-1)\cdot ||{r}_{x}\times {r}_{y}||\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(-x-y-1)\cdot 3\sqrt{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{1}{\cancel{\sqrt{2}}}(-x-y-1)\cdot 3\cancel{\sqrt{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & =-3{∬}_{D}(x+y+1)\,\text{d}A \\  & =-3{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}(x+y+1)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =-3{\int }_{0}^{4}{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+xy+x]}_{x=0}^{x=2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =-3{\int }_{0}^{4}(2y+4)\,\text{d}y \\  & =-3[{y}^{2}+4y]_{0}^{4} \\  & =-3\cdot 32 \\  & =-96\end{aligned}
